title: China And St. Augustine
gist: Gavekal's Louis-Vincent Gave notes that Chinese equities have fallen ten straight weeks for the first time ever, erasing recent outperformance despite the AI boom and China's AI gains, following a Beijing-engineered floor put under markets in January 2024 (teaser only; paywalled remainder).

themes.theme: Chinese equities after the policy put

insights.claim: Chinese equity markets have fallen for 10 consecutive weeks, a streak they had never previously recorded, wiping out their steady outperformance over the month, quarter, year-to-date and trailing 12 months.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: A record losing streak is a sentiment extreme worth watching as a contrarian or trend signal for China exposure.
insights.quote: Chinese equity markets have now fallen for 10 consecutive weeks, a feat they had never achieved before.

insights.claim: Chinese equities are falling despite AI excitement driving global equity performance and despite China being one of the few countries outside the US registering notable AI gains, implying the AI narrative is not currently supporting the market.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: The AI trade is not lifting China; positioning there is not following the global AI beta.

insights.claim: Beijing intervened in January 2024 to put a floor under domestic equities after deciding prices had fallen far enough, producing solid returns in 2024 and 2025, after having ended the 2015 bull market by pulling margin lending and imposing restrictions.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Chinese policy has repeatedly set both ceilings and floors; the returns of 2024–25 were policy-driven and have since faded.
